title: Simultaneous coefficient and pullback coherence of the Frobenius comparison
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, and the coefficient rings $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-pur-conventions], with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $n\geq1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}((z\mapsto z^q)^{-1})$, $\Phi_T=F_{T_0}^{(q)}\times_{k_0}k$, $G_T=Lg_T^*$ and $H_T=L\Phi_T^*$. On the small pro-etale coefficient categories of [def-pur-conventions] let $\kappa_{T,N}:H_TN\simeq G_TN$ be the specified comparison of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius], with the strict-tower, scalar-localized and common-stage constructions of [def-pur-tate-datum]. At finite coefficients this is the comparison induced from the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], whose relative-Frobenius maps on weakly etale objects $v:V\to T$ are $r_{V/T}^{(a)}=(F_V^a,v)$ as specified in [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback].

For any of the derived coefficient functors $C_T$ (finite quotient reduction, integral-to-finite reduction, finite integral extension with its actual quotient-tower comparisons, rationalization, finite field extension, or common-stage passage), let $j_H:C_TH_T\simeq H'_TC_T$ and $j_G:C_TG_T\simeq G'_TC_T$ be the canonical pullback/coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; primes indicate the changed coefficient stage. On their bounded constructible finite-Tor domains one has the equality of specified natural transformations
$$j_{G,N}C_T(\kappa_{T,N})=\kappa'_{T,C_TN}j_{H,N}.$$
For a morphism $u_0:T'_0\to T_0$ of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, let $u:T'\to T$ be its geometric base change. Write $c_H:Lu^*H_T\simeq H_{T'}Lu^*$ and $c_G:Lu^*G_T\simeq G_{T'}Lu^*$ for the canonical pullback compositors. Then
$$c_G(Lu^*\kappa_T)=(\kappa_{T'}Lu^*)c_H.$$
These coefficient and geometric equations are simultaneous: composing them in either order gives the same transformation under the canonical coefficient/pullback comparisons, and they obey identity and successive coefficient-change and pullback compositions. For a normalized actual integral reduction tower the finite equations are equations of maps of whole strict systems, including every transition and the inverse comparison, before applying derived inverse limit; the integral, rational and common-stage equations concern exactly their specified transports. On a tensor representative the coefficient square for site restriction has both values $r^*(x)\otimes b$ on $x\otimes b$.

For every morphism $z:N\to M$ on $T$ with data $\varphi_N:G_TN\to N$ and $\varphi_M:G_TM\to M$ satisfying $z\varphi_N=\varphi_MG_T(z)$, put $u_N=\varphi_N\kappa_{T,N}$ and $u_M=\varphi_M\kappa_{T,M}$. The actual comparisons satisfy
$$z u_N=z\varphi_N\kappa_{T,N}=\varphi_MG_T(z)\kappa_{T,N}=\varphi_M\kappa_{T,M}H_T(z)=u_MH_T(z).$$
This correspondence commutes with the coefficient and geometric comparison equations just displayed, with composition of equivariant arrows, and with pasting diagrams whose edges are such arrows and comparisons. It is a natural precomposition comparison, requiring no Cartesianity of the commuting scheme-Frobenius square.

proof.text: First work with finite constant rings. The relative-Frobenius isomorphisms in [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] specify a geometric inverse-image isomorphism, not an arbitrary equivalence. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-two-iso-scalar-pairing] to this isomorphism and any finite ring map A→B. Its balanced-pairing equation says that restriction along r commutes with scalar extension; on generalized tensor generators both routes send x⊗b to r^*(x)⊗b, and the inverse restriction obeys the same equation. This is a sheaf equation, not just an equation on constant global sections. The flat-term K-flat representative and mate normalization of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] derives this ordinary equation and identifies its scalar maps with the canonical derived comparisons. The expanded-composite clause of the pairing lemma and the composition clause of the normalization lemma apply to the specified factorization κ_T=(τ_T^(a)G_T)d_T of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius], where d_T:H_T≅L(F_T^a)^*G_T. Pasting the scalar squares for d_T and τ_T^(a)G_T proves j_G C(κ_T)=κ'_T C j_H. These are exactly the pullback comparisons named in [lem-fix-operation-reduction].

proof.text:
For an arbitrary u_0 as in the statement, naturality of absolute Frobenius gives uF_{T'}^a=F_T^a u; the geometric-Galois maps also commute with u, since u is base changed from k_0. Put P_T=L(F_T^a)^*. The specified factorization comparisons d_T satisfy
(P_{T'}c_G)(c_P G_T)(Lu^*d_T)=(d_{T'}Lu^*)c_H
by [lem-pur-factorized-pullback-square-pasting], with r=F^a, s=g and t=Φ. The factorization Φ=gF^a is the one specifying κ in [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Postcompose this equation with τ_{T'}^(a)G_{T'}Lu^*. Naturality of τ_{T'} moves c_G past τ_{T'}, and [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] replaces (τ_{T'}^(a)Lu^*)c_P by Lu^*τ_T^(a). The resulting equation is precisely c_G(Lu^*κ_T)=(κ_{T'}Lu^*)c_H. The arbitrary-pullback trivialization lemma applies to u itself; it has no smoothness hypothesis. Neither this argument nor the pasting lemma requires a Cartesian scheme-Frobenius square.

proof.text: The finite equations hold simultaneously. Expand each mixed coefficient/pullback route into the d and τ factors above. The expanded-composite scalar equation of [lem-sfb-geometric-two-iso-scalar-pairing], with the canonical derived normalization of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], identifies the two routes, including the commuting-square composition maps. In local restriction notation their common value is r^*(x)⊗b; naturality of r under base change is the equality used in step 2. For two coefficient maps A→B→D the common value is r^*(x)⊗bc on (x⊗b)⊗c. The strict coefficient unit and composition equations of [lem-pur-strict-coefficient-comparison-calculus] identify this with the single-change route, in both directions. For successive geometric pullbacks use the associativity equation of [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence]; each expanded route then has the same ordered factors d and τ. For the identity pullback its termwise identity comparison is [lem-pur-proetale-derived-pullback-identity]. Thus identity, successive-change, successive-pullback and mixed diagrams use the specified comparisons.

proof.text: For an actual integral reduction system choose one flat-term K-flat representative P and P_n=P⊗(A_{E,n})_T as prescribed by [def-pur-tate-datum]. At every degree, r and r inverse are the same site maps for every n. A quotient transition sends x⊗b to x⊗red(b), so restriction followed by transition and transition followed by restriction both give r^*(x)⊗red(b); the identical calculation holds for r inverse. These section restrictions commute with the cochain differential by naturality. The scalar/pullback maps and their inverses are strict system maps by [lem-pur-strict-coefficient-comparison-calculus]. The d maps are strict compositors by [lem-pur-normalized-pullback-composition-transport]. Consequently the finite equations of steps 1–3 are actual equalities of maps of these whole cochain systems, including inverse maps and all transitions, before localization. Apply the functorial Rlim of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The substitution comparisons of [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] identify the vertices and compositors with the specified completed operations, naturally for system morphisms. By the definition in [def-pur-tate-datum] the realized κ and its inverse are exactly the prescribed integral maps. This proves the integral geometric equations and their finite-reduction equations as coherent-system equations; no faithfulness of evaluation on derived morphisms is used.

proof.text: For E⊂L use the simultaneous quotient diagrams and the λ, μ comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. They specify the integral scalar/pullback comparison as μ^(-1)λ, using the counit of the whole system. At a quotient level step 1 applies to the actual map O_E/varpi_E^m→O_L/varpi_L^m. Restriction by r leaves both coefficient factors fixed, so it commutes with each normalized scalar map on generators and hence with the diagram counit by naturality. This proves equality of the simultaneous quotient diagrams defining the two scalar routes. The ramified identification in [lem-weil-ramified-pullback-tower-identification] distinguishes the scalar-extended E quotient from the L quotient: the former has index em, and its same-index map is the transition em→m. Step 4 shows compatibility with exactly that transition as well; no same-index quotient is declared an isomorphism. Realizing the diagram equation through λ and μ proves the required integral scalar square for κ. The composition/scalar, identity, successive-extension and arbitrary-iteration clauses of the realization lemma give the simultaneous geometric/scalar equations and their composition laws for these actual comparisons. Integral-to-finite reduction uses the original quotient system of step 4, with the substitution counits of [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], so it agrees with [lem-fix-operation-reduction] on the stated bounded constructible finite-Tor domains.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to the integral functors and transformations just constructed. Pullbacks and restriction along r are O_E-linear, and integral extension to L is semilinear for O_E→O_L, so the lemma applies. It preserves inverse transformations, compositions, whiskering and every displayed equality; this gives rationalization, finite field extension and all their mixed equations for the specified scalar-localized maps. For overline Q_l use [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: any finite diagram of objects and arrows is represented over one common finite field, and equality of representatives is tested after a further common extension. The equations already proved over that field therefore give exactly the specified common-stage transformations, independent of its enlargement, with their identity and composition laws. Restrict throughout to the bounded constructible finite-Tor domains of the statement; no discrete integral or rational coefficient category is substituted.

proof.text:
Naturality of the specified κ gives G_T(z)κ_{T,N}=κ_{T,M}H_T(z). Substitute this and the hypothesis zφ_N=φ_MG_T(z) to obtain, in order,
z u_N=zφ_Nκ_{T,N}=φ_MG_T(z)κ_{T,N}=φ_Mκ_{T,M}H_T(z)=u_MH_T(z).
The inverse correspondence is φ_N=u_Nκ_{T,N}^{-1}; the inverse naturality equation proves it on arrows as well. For coefficient change the transported datum is C(φ_N)j_{G,N}^{-1}, and precomposition gives
C(φ_N)j_{G,N}^{-1}κ'_{C N}=C(φ_N)C(κ_N)j_{H,N}^{-1}=C(u_N)j_{H,N}^{-1}
by the coefficient equation. The identical substitution with Lu^*, c_G and c_H proves geometric compatibility. For z:N→M and w:M→L, composing w u_M=u_LH(w) and z u_N=u_MH(z) gives (wz)u_N=u_LH(wz) by functoriality. A pasted diagram is treated one adjacent square at a time: replace each equivariant edge by the displayed naturality equation and each comparison edge by steps 1–6, and reassociate. Induction on the number of squares proves the claim for every finite pasting. These are formal substitutions in the natural transformations already constructed; no new base-change theorem is used.
